utterances.text: I recognise document 6.20. It is a decision of the President of the Executive Committee of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor, whereby deputy commander for the organisation and mobilisation and personal issues was relieved of his duty, it is Mr. Vahid Ceric, who is a Muslim by nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That position that Mr. Ceric was holding, is that a military or a civilian position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a civilian position, and the function, the duty of the official in this post is to conduct the mobilisation, to carry out the mobilisation. That's his most direct task. He's therefore a deputy to the commander who is in charge of organising mobilisation and other such activities. Paragraph 2 of the decision states the following: "This decision shall come into effect with the date of its issuance, and in charge of its implementation will be Major Zeljaja." That is a military person who at the time was the commander of the garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now, in normal times, prior to this take-over on the 20th of April, based on your knowledge of the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina, would it be normal for the President of an Executive Committee to give a direction to a military commander of a JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. The question calls for expertise in law and so has been addressed. The witness's occurrence with this is -- not an expert of law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can explore with the witness if he can answer the question or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But if he is not an expert in law, then he probably can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, as a member of parliament in Bosnia-Herzegovina and given the development during the time you were elected of the state -- the development of the state as an independent state, was it a matter for you to become familiar with the operation of the different branches of government, the roles and responsibilities of the various branches, both on the republic and municipal level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was. As a member of the parliament of the Republic, I had to discuss proposals, drafts of the law, and I participated in these discussions; and during my mandate, we adopted several hundreds of amendments to already existing laws and laws themselves. Members of parliament are not exclusively lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Semenovic, during the course of your creation of the new state, did you discuss in these amendments which you referred to the separations between the various branches and organisations in the government as it existed in the former Yugoslavia, that is, the differences between civilian elected officials, the Ministry of the Interior, the police forces, and the military and what the separations of powers and authority were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we discussed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has given sufficient evidence to enable his reply to remain on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In your opinion and based on your background then, would this indicate that the accused, in signing this directive, was exercising authority which normally did not accompany his office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could we now move to 6.17? Do you recognise the name of the person in paragraph 1, or can you determine his ethnic background or national background from his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Mr. Bucan Iso. I didn't know him personally, but judging by the name and surname, I suppose he's a Bosniak Muslim and I'm sure he's not of Serbian descent. He is relieved of his capacity and function as the Commander of the Rear, and the decision comes into force on the date of adoption, and it will be implemented by Major Zeljaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now, this post that Iso Bucan held, Commander for the Security of the Rear, do you know whether that was a military or a civilian position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was a civilian or a military function. I suppose it was a military function; however, functionally, it covered the intelligence area of the civilian sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Again, is the fact that this document is making Major Zeljaja responsible for its implementation an exercise of power that would not normally come with the office of the accused at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, these documents are documents 2.11, 2.12, and 2.14. They all relate, in fact, to the same decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, but they're being offered for slightly different reasons, which I will explain through the witness, but they can be considered collectively as they reflect the same information. These are documents that were not agreed to by the parties for admission, Your Honour, as we had not got to this category.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, if you could look at number 2.12 first, please, which, on the second page of the document, is a newspaper article which is publishing this act of the Autonomous Region Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this decision of the Autonomous Region Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, I don't have clear markings on top. Is that a document that's entitled "Rukovodioci-Samo Lojalni Srbi"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, were you familiar with this decision or the content of this decision back in June of '92 when this was issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I would direct your attention to paragraph 1 of the decision.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 of this decision imposes that on all leading positions, positions involving access to information, protection of public property and other positions of importance for the functioning of the economy can be occupied exclusively by personnel of Serbian nationality. It applies to all socially-owned enterprises, joint stock companies, state institutions, public enterprises, the Minister of the Interior, and the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In addition, such positions cannot be occupied by workers who have not confirmed their Serbian nationality in the plebiscite or to whom it is not yet clear that the only representative of the Serbian people is the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Does that indicate to you that the decision is not simply that positions may only be held by the Serbs but it's defining what Serbs are loyal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Keegan, that really is a leading question. Anyway, I think that's probably a matter for us to determine, not the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then if you look to paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 says that: "Failure to carry out the above Decision shall result in automatic suspension of the responsible persons."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now, if you look to the document marked 2.11?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before you get to that, there is a third page attached to the document which I have at 2.12. That is the decision you've referred to. Then there is the original, I take it, and then there's a third page --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That is the translation, Your Honour, of the actual news part of the article that's at the top of the decision. I was referring only to the decision itself with this witness. I thought, again, a news article is fairly self-explanatory in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we move to 2.11, and Mr. Semenovic, does the first page reflect the same decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And then on the second page, can you identify that document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second page, we have again a conclusion of the Crisis Staff, the meeting held on the 23rd of June, 1992. At meetings of the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality held on the 23rd of June, it was decided that we forward you the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina for implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who is that document signed by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was signed by Dr. Milomir Stakic, President of the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then if we could move to 2.14, and does that document, on the first page, reflect reproduction of the same decision of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: On the second page, does it indicate who is forwarding that decision and what their organisation is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the second page, yes, on the second page, it says that, in the implementation of this, the chiefs of public security stations are obliged to particularly abide by its provisions with regard to the proposal of candidates for posts described in Article 1 of the decision. The reason for this is the fact that the CSB has the authority to decide on the appointments and placement of staff while the chiefs of SJBs nominate the candidate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What does the last paragraph of that section say, just above the signature block, beginning with "In the same fashion"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says that: "In the same fashion, when recommending new staff for certain posts, particular attention must be paid to the provisions of section 1, paragraph 3 of the decision: 'Chiefs of public security stations will be responsible for the above.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Again, paragraph 3 of section 1 of the decision is which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, section 1, it's section -- I don't see the third paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, are we looking at 2.14?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: If you could please ask counsel to lead us through these documents because I'm clearly not following. It seems the witness is having some difficulties too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: On the first page in the Serbian version, Mr. Semenovic, what you have is section 1, and you see two paragraphs. Then it appears there's a page number inserted, which is 2, but that's not actually section 2, that's the third paragraph of section 1, because below that you see the double Roman (ii) for section 2. So it's confusing in the fact that they apparently submitted a page number --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: The Serbo Croatian is illegible. I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do understand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be as well, if this document is looked at again, and the original be shown to the Defence so they can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, it is now five to five in any event. I understand there is a matter that you want to raise in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is that right? Well, that might be a convenient moment. Are there many more documents you want to produce?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, there are, but perhaps, since we will be on break over the next couple of days, I can meet with Defence counsel to see if we can stipulate on admission on the foundational matters, and therefore, I'll just have to go directly to the point of the document with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That seems a sensible course. Mr. Semenovic, would you be back, please, on Monday morning at half past nine, and you're free to go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Your Honour. I will, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: We did wish to do this as a matter in closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can we go into closed session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Whereupon proceedings adjourned at 5.15 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 13th day of July, 1998 at 9.30 a.m.
